notes: Gypsum board partition wall. Cross-checked: published 0.29/0.10/0.05/0.04/0.07/0.09 agrees on shape, low band varies with cavity depth.
Hard mineral wall. Near-total reflector at all bands.
Glazed tile or marble. The hardest common surface; bathroom and kitchen walls.
Single glazing. Published low band ranges 0.10-0.35 depending on pane size and mounting.
Glass bonded to a wall, so the panel resonance that lifts a free window low band is suppressed.
Solid wood 1.6 cm. Doors, table tops, cabinet carcasses.
Thin panel over an air gap; the low band rises because the panel resonates.
Wood flooring on joists.
Pile carpet with underlay. The dominant floor absorber in a furnished home.
Thin rug laid directly on a hard floor, no underlay.
Draped, folded fabric hung clear of the wall.
Thin unlined fabric; a much weaker absorber than it looks.
Unoccupied upholstered seating. Sofas and armchairs, the main mid-band absorber in a living room.
Thicker and denser than seat upholstery, so slightly better at low frequency.
Pillows, blankets, towels, clothing. Porous and light, so weak below 250 Hz.
Stuffed toys and similar. Small, so their total area matters more than their coefficient.
Tables, chairs, shelving and cabinets seen as a whole object.
Appliance casings, racks, railings. Reflective across the band.
Metal cabinet with some internal damping and vents; fridges, ovens, washers.
Sanitary ware, crockery, vases. Effectively a perfect reflector.
Filled bath or sink. Listed for completeness; the area involved is small.
Books on open shelves, stacked paper. Absorbs mainly at high frequency.
Potted plants and foliage. High scattering, low absorption, and acoustically near transparent at low frequency because the leaves are far smaller than the wavelength.
Mineral fibre ceiling tile. Used for the ceiling surface, not for objects.
A person, as the difference between an occupied and an empty upholstered seat.
Fallback for small dense objects with no better match. Deliberately reflective: assuming absorption we cannot justify would flatter the room.
Fallback for objects that are clearly textile or porous but have no specific entry.
